Compute inside Arrow with dplyr

arrow-native.Rmd

Spatial functions that run in Arrow’s query engine, not in R.

Why it matters: a Dataset can be larger than memory. If every spatial call drags the geometry column into R, that advantage is gone.

library(geoarrowrs)
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(geoarrow)

The problem

Arrow only knows the functions registered with it. Call anything else and it gives up and pulls your data into R.

nc <- as.data.frame(read_shapefile(
  system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf")
))
tbl <- arrow_table(nc)

Without registration you get a warning and a fallback:

Warning: Expression not supported in Arrow
→ Pulling data into R

On a Table that is merely slow. On a Dataset that does not fit in memory, it fails outright.

The fix

One call.

registered <- register_geoarrow_udfs(tbl)
#> Warning: Could not register 5 functions for this geometry type.
#> ℹ `length_euclidean()`, `length_haversine()`, `length_geodesic()`,
#>   `length_rhumb()`, and `length_vincenty()`
#> ✖ First reason: Invalid argument error: Extension type name mismatch: expected
#>   geoarrow.linestring, got geoarrow.multipolygon
length(registered)
#> [1] 46

Now the same code runs inside the engine.

tbl |>
  mutate(area = unsigned_area(geometry)) |>
  select(NAME, area) |>
  head(3) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   NAME        area
#>   <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 Ashe      0.114 
#> 2 Alleghany 0.0614
#> 3 Surry     0.143

It composes

Filter on a spatial predicate. The comparison happens in the engine.

tbl |>
  filter(unsigned_area(geometry) > 0.1) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>       n
#>   <int>
#> 1    66

Geometry in, geometry out. The result keeps its GeoArrow type.

res <- tbl |>
  mutate(centre = centroid(geometry)) |>
  select(NAME, centre) |>
  head(3) |>
  collect()

class(res$centre)
#> [1] "geoarrow_vctr"  "nanoarrow_vctr"

Predicates take two geometry columns.

tbl |>
  mutate(self = intersects(geometry, geometry)) |>
  summarise(all_true = all(self)) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   all_true
#>   <lgl>   
#> 1 TRUE

Datasets stream

This is the case that matters. Nothing here holds the whole column in memory.

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "nc-dataset")
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
write_dataset(tbl, dir, format = "feather")

open_dataset(dir, format = "feather") |>
  filter(unsigned_area(geometry) > 0.1) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>       n
#>   <int>
#> 1    66

What gets registered

46 of 51 functions register against a multipolygon column. The rest are skipped on purpose, and the warning tells you which:

  • Wrong geometry type. length_euclidean() needs linestrings. Against multipolygons there is nothing to measure, so it is not registered.
  • Non-geometry arguments. buffer() and simplify() take a distance. Arrow kernels here only take geometry columns.
  • Aggregates. unary_union() collapses an array to one row. That is not a scalar kernel.

Arrow dispatches on the exact input type, so a kernel is registered for the precise GeoArrow type in your data. Reading a different geometry type means calling register_geoarrow_udfs() again with that data.

Use prefix if a name would collide with an existing Arrow binding:

head(register_geoarrow_udfs(tbl, prefix = "geo_"), 3)
#> Warning: Could not register 5 functions for this geometry type.
#> ℹ `length_euclidean()`, `length_haversine()`, `length_geodesic()`,
#>   `length_rhumb()`, and `length_vincenty()`
#> ✖ First reason: Invalid argument error: Extension type name mismatch: expected
#>   geoarrow.linestring, got geoarrow.multipolygon
#> [1] "geo_signed_area"    "geo_unsigned_area"  "geo_signed_area_cd"

The bottom line

Register once, then write ordinary dplyr. The geometry stays in Arrow and the work happens in the engine.
